definitions.explanation: Words of praise that may not be entirely sincere, often said to please someone or be polite.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}でもうれしいです。
examples.english: Even if it's just flattery, I'm happy to hear it.

examples.japanese: お{世辞|せじ}を{言|い}うのが{上手|じょうず}な{人|ひと}だ。
お{世辞|せじ}にも{上手|うま}いとは{言|い}えない。
examples.english: I can't say it's good, even as a compliment.
examples.notes: Set phrase for 'not even being polite can make it good.'

notes:
FORMATION:
お (polite prefix) + {世辞|せじ} (compliments)

The plain form {世辞|せじ} exists but お{世辞|せじ} is much more common.

COLLOCATIONS:
・お{世辞|せじ}を{言|い}う - to pay compliments
・お{世辞|せじ}にも〜ない - can't say ~ even as flattery
・お{世辞|せじ}{抜|ぬ}きで - frankly, without flattery
・{社交|しゃこう}{辞令|じれい} - social pleasantries

SIMILAR WORDS:
・おべっか - brown-nosing, sucking up
・{追従|ついしょう} - flattery (formal)
・{褒|ほ}め{言葉|ことば} - words of praise (more sincere)
